text:
emily: Quick thread 1: propose a new mid-market SKU 'PulsePack' to give customers predictable monthly units with per-route allocations, optional priority lanes, and clearer rollover rules. Want product + eng + sales alignment before I write PRD.

ravi: curious 0: how is this materially different from FlexCredits/burst packs?

emily: short: PulsePack focuses on per-route budgeting (customers can assign X pulses to route A, Y to route B), built-in auto-topup add-on, and flexible rollover banking up to 2 months for GA. It's intended for teams who manage multiple LLM features and need routing-level guarantees.

claire-sales: sales needs a one-liner and a sample FAQ. Also: can we carve out priority lanes only for a subset of routes? customers ask for that.

emily: yes, priority can be per-route as an add-on. Sketch below:
```
PulsePack v1.0 (pricing sketch)
- Starter: 8,000 pulses / month @ $400 (bank up to 1 month)
- Pro: 40,000 pulses / month @ $1,750 (bank up to 2 months)
- Enterprise: custom pulses + negotiated price + optional guaranteed priority lanes
- Mapping: 1 pulse ~= 4k tokens (customer-configurable mapping)
- Overage: $0.055 / pulse until softcap (softcap = 25% of monthly allocation) then overflow rate $0.095/pulse OR auto-fallback to cheaper model if enabled
- Add-ons: per-route priority lane (+20% on pack price for routes opted-in), auto-topup (card-on-file) for immediate refill, cross-route pooling (opt-in)
- Contract constraints: pulses are non-transferable between orgs; rollover banking limited to X months (see plan); no retroactive rate changes during active contract term
```

ravi: eng notes 1: implementation surface: quota service needs per-route sub-buckets, UI for admins to allocate pulses to routes, billing flow for auto-topup, and runtime enforcement to honor priority lanes. Also need metrics: usage by pulse, tokens, route, model variant. Biggest unknown: complexity of per-route KV caching impact if we start doing strict route isolation.

olga: product ops 2: revenue recognition / accounting: credits sold as deferred revenue; auto-topup can complicate month boundaries (we'll need clear invoice rules). Also confirm whether unused banked pulses expire after the banking window. For GA product ops prefers fixed expiry policy (e.g., bank up to 2 months then oldest expire).

nate: legal 3: contract language checklist: define "pulse" clearly (token mapping and runtime exceptions), define rollover rules (max months banked), define priority lane SLAs and what happens on capacity constraints, and a clause about overage invoice disputes. Also we should block pilots if they demand transferability or resale of pulses.

claire-sales: pilot candidates: EchoServe (fintech), BrightForms (forms SaaS), AtlasMaps (location analytics) 1 think EchoServe will push for per-route isolation and guaranteed latency on key endpoints.

emily: proposed launch criteria (GA gating):
- billing: per-route buckets + rollover logic implemented, auto-topup flow wired to payments and invoice line-items
- console: admin UI to allocate pulses to routes and enable priority lanes; API support for programmatic allocation
- legal: standard T&Cs including pulse definition and rollover expiry approved
- pilots: 3 signed pilots with baseline usage metrics and acceptance criteria (latency, availability, billing reconciliation)
- telemetry: dashboards for pulse consumption by route/model, alerting on >90% consumption and softcap breaches
- docs: AE one-pager, customer FAQ, and sample contract clause snippets

ravi: rough timeline 4: baseline MVP (no auto-topup, no cross-route pooling) = 7 weeks if we: reuse billing overage path, reuse existing priority routing infra, and ship a simple console page. Add-ons (auto-topup, pooling) = +2-4 weeks. Per-route strict cache isolation = risky for MVP.

olga: operational callouts 5: need a test harness to validate banking/expiry across monthly boundaries; billing QA will need synthetic accounts. Also add a reconciliation job to tag expired pulses for accounting.

nate: add legal requirement: pilot agreements must include a clause that pilot pricing is provisional and GA pricing may differ with 30 days notice. Ops: require opt-in for auto-topup for pilots.

claire-sales: messaging suggestion: "PulsePack 200: predictable monthly units, allocate by feature, avoid surprise bills." I'll draft a short pitch and a pricing table once PRD is up. :rocket:

emily: any objections to banking up to 2 months for Pro for GA? otherwise we'll default to 1 month across Starter.

ravi: no tech objections from infra side.

olga: ops ok with 2 months for Pro but insist on deterministic expiry logic.

nate: legal OK as long as we have explicit expiry language and overage dispute process.

emily: thanks everyone. Next steps: I'll draft PRD and include an MVP tech appendix. I'll schedule a sync with @ravi and @olga for scoping tomorrow 9:30am PT. I'll post the PRD link here when ready.
